original_question: Does Table 1 in the survey give a complete classification, up to the exponent equivalence relation of Definition 5.7, of all pairs (F, d) where F is a finite field, d is an invertible exponent over F, and the Weil spectrum W_{F,d} is three-valued?
target_in_paper: Open Problem 10.17 in Section 10: "Is every pair (F, d) of finite field and invertible exponent such that W_{F,d} is three-valued accounted for (up to the equivalence of Definition 5.7) on Table 1?"
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's exact target. It correctly focuses on Table 1, on pairs (F, d) with F a finite field and d an invertible exponent, on the three-valued condition for W_{F,d}, and on quotienting by the exponent-equivalence relation from Definition 5.7. In substance, it is essentially a paraphrase of Open Problem 10.17.
missing_details: The paper defines W_{F,d} as the function a -> sum_{x in F} psi(x^d - ax), where psi is the canonical additive character of F; this should be stated explicitly to make the question stand-alone (Definition 1.3).
Strictly speaking, the Weil spectrum is the set {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*}; the paper then says "W_{F,d} is three-valued" as shorthand for that spectrum having cardinality 3 (Definitions 1.4 and 10.1).
An invertible exponent over F means a positive integer d with gcd(d, |F^*|) = 1 (Definition 1.1).

The equivalence relation should be spelled out: d and e are equivalent over F if d ≡ p^k e or d ≡ p^k e^{-1} (mod |F^*|) for some integer k, where p = char(F) and e^{-1} is taken modulo |F^*| (Definition 5.7).

The official wording is "accounted for on Table 1" rather than the broader phrase "gives a complete classification"; the latter is reasonable, but the former is the paper-faithful formulation (Open Problem 10.17).

The nearby context distinguishes this from the narrower Helleseth Three-Valued Conjecture, which asks only about nonexistence when [F:F_p] is a power of 2; Open Problem 10.17 asks for all three-valued pairs, up to equivalence (Conjecture 10.6 and Open Problem 10.17).
refined_question: Let F be a finite field of characteristic p with canonical additive character psi, let d be a positive integer with gcd(d, |F^*|) = 1, and define W_{F,d}(a) = sum_{x in F} psi(x^d - ax) for a in F. Write the Weil spectrum as {W_{F,d}(a) : a in F^*}, and say that W_{F,d} is three-valued if this set has cardinality 3. If d and e are invertible exponents over F, say they are equivalent when d ≡ p^k e or d ≡ p^k e^{-1} (mod |F^*|) for some integer k. Is every pair (F, d) for which W_{F,d} is three-valued accounted for, up to this equivalence, by one of the entries in Table 1?
justification: The draft is aimed at the paper's exact classification-style open problem, not merely at a neighboring conjecture. In Section 10, after defining what it means for W_{F,d} to be k-valued and explaining that Table 1 records the known three-valued cases, Katz states Open Problem 10.17 asking whether every pair (F, d) with W_{F,d} three-valued is accounted for on Table 1 up to Definition 5.7. Definitions 1.3 and 1.4 provide the meaning of W_{F,d} and its Weil spectrum, Definition 10.1 gives the exact meaning of "three-valued," and Definition 5.7 gives the exponent-equivalence relation. The surrounding discussion also shows that this is broader than Conjecture 10.6: Conjecture 10.6 asks only for nonexistence in the case [F:F_p] a power of 2, whereas Open Problem 10.17 asks for a complete accounting of all three-valued pairs.
